abstract: It has been recognized that the tumour markers alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) and human chorionic gonadotrophin (HCG) may show a transient elevation after the initiation of chemotherapy in non-seminomatous testicular cancer. We investigated the prognostic importance of these so-called marker surges in a cohort of patients treated with cisplatin combination chemotherapy between 1983 and 1991. A total of 669 patients were studied. Of 352 patients who had an elevated AFP at the start of treatment and for whom we had data at both day 1 and day 8, 101 (29%) had a surge. Of 317 patients for whom we had data for HCG, 80 patients (25%) had a surge. It was found that an AFP surge was a strong adverse prognostic factor for progression [hazard ratio (HR) 2.28, P=0.005]. There was no statistically significant difference in survival (HR 1.65, P=0.13). There was no prognostic significance of a HCG surge, either for progression or for survival. To investigate whether a surge was an independent prognostic factor for progression and survival, multivariate Cox regression models were fitted using the independent prognostic factors for progression and survival and the surge/decline variable. An AFP surge was retained in the final model for progression. A HCG surge was of no prognostic importance for progression or survival. We conclude that an AFP surge has an adverse prognostic significance, independent of pretreatment characteristics.
abstract_ja: 非セミノーマ性精巣がんの患者で、化学療法開始後にみられる腫瘍マーカーAFPおよびヒト絨毛性ゴナドトロピン(hCG)の一過性上昇(サージ)の予後的意義を検討した。1983年から1991年にシスプラチン併用化学療法を受けた669例を対象とした。治療開始時にAFPが上昇していた352例のうち101例(29%)にAFPサージがみられ、AFPサージは増悪に対する強い不良予後因子であった(ハザード比2.28、P=0.005)。全生存については有意差は認められなかった。hCGサージには増悪・生存のいずれにも予後的意義はなかった。多変量Cox回帰解析の結果、AFPサージは増悪に対する独立した予後因子として残存した。以上より、AFPサージは治療前因子とは独立して不良な予後的意義を持つと結論された。
